claim: Dapagliflozin reduces heart-failure hospitalization or cardiovascular death in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
gold_rationale: This is settled clinical/regulatory consensus. The pivotal DAPA-HF RCT (McMurray, NEJM 2019; N=4744 HFrEF with and without diabetes) tested the EXACT claimed composite primary endpoint — worsening HF (hospitalization/urgent HF visit) or CV death — and showed a highly significant 26% relative reduction (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.65-0.85, p<0.001), with benefit consistent regardless of diabetes status. The FDA approved dapagliflozin (Farxiga) for HFrEF on 5 May 2020 specifically to reduce the risk of CV death and HF hospitalization, based on DAPA-HF — direct regulatory endorsement of the claim. The independent EMPEROR-Reduced RCT (Packer, NEJM 2020; empagliflozin, N=3730) confirmed a class effect on the same composite endpoint (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.65-0.86), and the prospective Zannad IPD meta-analysis (Lancet 2020) pooling both trials confirmed reductions in CV death or HF hospitalization. Every pivotal trial measured the claimed hard-outcome composite directly (no surrogate substitution), all point the same direction, and the finding is enshrined in ACC/AHA/HFSA and ESC guidelines as a Class I recommendation for HFrEF. No contradicting RCT exists.
outcome: Composite of worsening heart failure event (HF hospitalization or urgent HF visit) or cardiovascular death
population: HFrEF (LVEF <=40%, NYHA II-IV), with and without type 2 diabetes

rows.citation: McMurray JJV, Solomon SD, Inzucchi SE, et al. Dapagliflozin in Patients with Heart Failure and Reduced Ejection Fraction (DAPA-HF). N Engl J Med. 2019;381(21):1995-2008. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1911303
rows.integrity_note: Landmark pivotal double-blind placebo-controlled RCT (NCT03036124); PubMed article types confirm 'Randomized Controlled Trial' + 'Clinical Trial, Phase III'; not retracted; formed basis of FDA HFrEF approval.
rows.finding: Primary composite of worsening HF or CV death occurred in 16.3% (dapagliflozin) vs 21.2% (placebo); HR 0.74 (95% CI 0.65-0.85, p<0.001). Benefit consistent with and without diabetes. Primary endpoint IS the claimed composite (hard outcome, not surrogate).

rows.integrity_note: Registry entry verified: N=4744, PHASE3, double-blind placebo-controlled, HFrEF (LVEF<=40%, NYHA II-IV), pre-specified primary endpoint = worsening HF or CV death (exactly the claimed outcome), status COMPLETED.

rows.integrity_note: Independent pivotal RCT of a different SGLT2 inhibitor (empagliflozin, NCT03057977); PubMed article type 'Randomized Controlled Trial'; confirms class effect. Not retracted.
rows.finding: Primary composite of CV death or HF hospitalization: HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.65-0.86, p<0.001) in HFrEF (N=3730). Corroborates the claimed outcome as an SGLT2-inhibitor class effect; primary endpoint IS the claimed composite.

rows.citation: Zannad F, Ferreira JP, Pocock SJ, et al. SGLT2 inhibitors in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: a meta-analysis of the EMPEROR-Reduced and DAPA-HF trials. Lancet. 2020;396(10254):819-829. DOI:10.1016/S0140-6736(20)31824-9
rows.integrity_note: Pre-specified prospective individual-patient-data meta-analysis pooling the two pivotal HFrEF RCTs (N=8474); PubMed article type 'Meta-Analysis'; highest-tier evidence synthesis.
rows.finding: Pooled SGLT2 inhibitors reduced CV death or first HF hospitalization (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.68-0.82) and CV death alone (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.76-0.98) in HFrEF, consistent across diabetes status. Directly supports the claimed composite outcome.

baseline.text: Yes. Dapagliflozin reduces the composite of heart-failure hospitalization or cardiovascular death in HFrEF. This was established by the pivotal DAPA-HF trial (NEJM 2019), which randomized 4,744 patients with HFrEF (with and without type 2 diabetes) and found a 26% relative risk reduction in the primary composite of worsening heart failure or CV death (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.65-0.85). The FDA approved dapagliflozin for this indication in 2020, and the finding was corroborated as a class effect by EMPEROR-Reduced (empagliflozin) and confirmed in meta-analysis. It is a Class I guideline-recommended therapy for HFrEF.
